newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: FOCUS - Heineken profit warning hits shares.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Heineken profit warning hits shares.

text.p: Investors savaged Heineken shares on Friday after the Dutch brewing giant posted a first half net profit of 297 million guilders ($175.2 million), below analysts' expectations, and added to disappointment with a profit warning.
Heineken shares plunged 33.40 guilders, or over nine percent, to 329.30 guilders in early trading.
The company said it expected 1996 full-year net profit to be "somewhat" lower than 1995's 664 million guilders, blaming stagnant markets in its key European markets.
"Heineken does not expect beer markets in Europe to grow, which will lead to increasing pressure on margins," the company said in a statement.

It added that fine summer weather in 1995 meant sales volume in Europe appeared lower this year. It said cost increases in these markets could not be fully recovered through selling prices and the standard beer sector in particular was under pressure.

But this would be partly offset by a rise in exports and activities outside Europe. Sales in the Asia Pacific region had showed a clear increase over the six-month period to 690 million guilders from 593 million in the same 1995 period.
"Both the higher sales by local breweries and the rise in exports, especially to China and Taiwan, explained this increase," it said.
But analysts, saying the results themselves were not too disappointing, focused more on the profit warning, which they highlighted as the shock factor in the news.
"The expectation's the thing that's going to go against them, the figures weren't too awful," one said.
Dealers in Amsterdam warned that the shares could take another hammering later on Friday when U.S. markets open.
Marius Andre, analyst at Amstgeld, said he was cutting his 1996 full year net forecast to 650 million guilders from a previous 750 million.
"The real hiccup for Heineken is in Europe and there it's clear that the overall market is shrinking and already fierce competition is getting worse, putting pressure on margins."
"That of course is a big problem because that's where by far most of the business is generated," he said.
Half-year profits were up six percent on the 280 million guilders posted in the same period of 1995 but below the range forecast by analysts between 308 and 322 million guilders.

The group posted a 20.1 percent increase in turnover to 5.92 billion guilders, and a 7.7 percent increase in trading profit to 464 million. Net profit per share rose to 5.92 guilders from 5.59 in the same year ago period.
Heineken announced an unchanged interim dividend of 1.50 guilders per share.
